paragraphs: Here's what jumps out at me, friend. Joab does the hard work. He fights, he captures the royal fortress, he takes the water supply (2 Samuel 12:26-27). Then he sends word to David to come finish it, because otherwise the city "will be named after me" (2 Samuel 12:28). I think Joab knew exactly whose name belonged on that victory, and he gave the credit away.

Now look at the other side. David gathers the troops, takes the city, and the crown ends up on his head (2 Samuel 12:29-30). I bet that crown felt mighty good up there. That's the part I want you to sit with, baker. A win can feel so good that you forget how much of it came from other people's work, and I've seen a cookie take a bow that the whole batch earned.

So here's the big idea. Success comes with a pull toward the spotlight, and this passage shows us both the person who steps back and the person who steps up to wear the crown. The passage also shows that David puts the Ammonites to work with saws, iron picks and axes, and that's a heavy moment (2 Samuel 12:31). Today, ask who really did the work behind your wins, and keep your hands open to share the credit. The story isn't over, and there's more still to come.
